senses.gloss:
Guḍimallam
------------------------------------------
God being nirākāra (formless) and nirguṇa (without attributes) a symbol of rounded surface is, perhaps, the nearest iconic representation of his. A लिङ्ग or शिवलिङ्ग is exactly that. However phallic association of the लिङ्ग cannot also be ruled out since it might have been present in some aboriginal cults which might have been, later on, absorbed into the Vedic fold. The earliest शिवलिङ्ग discovered so far is at the Paraśurāmeśvara temple of गुडिमल्लम्, a village situated about ten kilometres from Renigunta in Andhra Pradesh. This is an unmistakable piece of iconic representation of शिवलिङ्ग as an erect phallus. It is 1.5 metres (5ft.) tall and is assigned to the period 100-200 B. C. A beautifully carved image of शिव standing against it and trampling a rākṣasa (demon), the apasmāra पुरुष (cretinous person), is an added attraction.
See also ŚIVALIṄGA.
